descriptionChirho: Hiram (also spelled Huram, Chiram) — a proper name referring to (a) the king of Tyre who was an ally of David and Solomon, supplying materials and craftsmen for the Temple (1 Kgs 5; 2 Chr 2), and (b) the skilled bronze artisan sent by King Hiram to Solomon (1 Kgs 7:13-45; 2 Chr 4:11-16). English 'Hiram/to Hiram/[Chiram],' Spanish 'Hiram/Jiram,' Hindi हीराम/हूराम, Arabic حيرام, Korean 히람, Swahili Hiramu. The two clusters differ only in spelling variant (Hiram vs Chiram/Huram) reflecting textual traditions, not distinct referents.
